title: 2nd Sitting of 1st Session of 2025
presiding: Speaker Abdul Raheem Abdulla opened the sitting; Deputy Speaker Ahmed Nazim took the chair during the urgent-matter debate and was presiding at the end of this part
summary: The sitting opened with 54 members present, 4 on leave and 12 on official travel. Members voted 63-0 to take up an urgent matter from the South Galolhu member on the government's handling of the December 2024 taxi drivers' protest; MDP members said a peaceful protest was obstructed and urged action on drivers' concerns, while PNC members said police acted calmly and that road closures hurt other residents. The chair then read presidential letters on ministry changes, a pay cut for heads of independent institutions and several nominations, each sent to a committee, and a bill amending the Decentralisation Act had its first reading. Debate then began on a resolution from the Kendhoo member calling for a common grooming and dress code for tourism staff (burqa, beards), and it continues into part 2. Some speaker headers are jumbled in the text layer, so a few turns may be misattributed. This part opens in the middle of a speech from part 1 and then continues the debate on item 8.1, a resolution from the member for Kendhoo asking the government to set a general grooming and dress standard for tourism workers so that staff can wear the hijab and keep beards. Members spoke for and around the resolution, with some arguing about whether it needed Majlis time. After a recess the Majlis began the debate on item 8.2, the government's gang crimes and other dangerous crimes bill, then paused it for voting. The resolution was accepted 60 to 0 and sent to the Economic Committee, and the next sitting was set for Tuesday 11 February 2025 at 9:00. The text layer is garbled in places, so speaker gists are approximate.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Raised points of order disputing a claim that drivers were given a protest area, saying the announced area was not allowed and they were forced onto the road.
Said drivers were consulted on a possible taxi line and meters, then a new taxi line was announced, threatening about 1,100 drivers' income; a petition went unanswered.
Tabled the dress code resolution citing Articles 19 and 37, and said about 45 percent of resorts now allow beards, citing a tourism employees' study.
As proposer, thanked members and recalled the earlier petition, draft regulation and circular to resorts under the MDP government.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Said all workers' rights should be protected but protests must be peaceful, and that road closures disrupted hospital access, travel and students.
Argued that rights belong to all residents and that the urgent matter was brought by MDP to encourage unlawful protest.
On the dress code resolution, said resorts set grooming rules staff accept when hired and urged consulting industry leaders rather than Parliament deciding.
Backed the bill, citing deaths and attacks linked to gangs and weapons, and said drug supply should also be tackled.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Said the government is working on taxi drivers' problems, pointed to election results, and criticised MDP's past record and its choice to table urgent matters.
Raised a point of order on the one-hour debate limit having passed; the chair set the time and continued.
Said he does not believe resorts ban beards or hijab and that MDP members could have raised it with ministers first.
Backed the gang crimes bill, thanked the sponsor, and hoped it would pass quickly after committee review.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Proposed the urgent matter, saying the government obstructed the taxi drivers' peaceful protest and detained drivers, and asking for their rights to be respected.
Said the government's early actions, including blocking unregistered newspapers, show disregard for protest and expression rights; criticised the transport minister's handling.
Raised a point of order objecting to remarks about members' age; the chair ruled it was not a point of order.

speakers.name: Abdulla Rifau
positions: Said drivers' and passengers' rights both matter, past governments did little, and the taxi sector needs regulation such as tracking devices and set hours.
Supported the resolution, saying tourism workers contribute greatly to the economy and grooming standards go beyond shaving.
Said the President's manifesto shows the government will look after tourism workers' rights and welfare.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Said no past government resolved taxi drivers' problems, including two MDP terms, and the closure of the main road affected many residents.
Said MDP's concern for drivers and resort workers is not sincere and cited police injuries during protests.
On the dress code resolution, supported it, noting the country is entirely Muslim; his turn continues into part 2.

speakers.name: Hussain Imran Latheef
positions: Said Islam permits beards and hijab, backed the resolution, and raised alcohol serving by Maldivian resort staff and the flat list timing before Ramadan.
Raised a point of order that no MDP member was in the chamber after the urgent matter was submitted.
On the gang bill, said root causes are housing and schools and asked that the committee stage not simply criminalise youth.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Muhammad
positions: Questioned the motion's purpose, asked about justice for a driver killed in 2019, and said about 1,480 active drivers do not represent the city's residents.
Supported the resolution but said the matter should be settled with the ministry and stakeholders rather than take Majlis time.
Recalled MDP's 2020 congress remarks on resort staff and questioned why the matter was raised now.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Said he did not support the motion, citing Constitution Article 70 and arguing one person's freedom ends where another's rights begin.
Supported the resolution and said dress and grooming standards for workers should follow the limits set by Islam.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Said Hulhumale' taxi parking and registration problems have been neglected for years, protests and road closures both need balance, and institutions should address drivers' concerns.
On the dress code resolution, supported it, saying staff should not be forced to shave beards and that Parliament should not require otherwise.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Supported extending the debate time so all members who asked to speak could do so; the chair did not accept it as a motion.
Supported the resolution, saying many resorts already allow it and young people in his area want a solution.
Expressed regret at remarks by some PNC members about MDP members.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Said tourism staff should be able to keep beards under clear rules and expects the President's government to resolve it.
Backed the gang crimes bill, noting the 2010 gang law has not delivered results and urging quick passage.

speakers.name: Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim
positions: Said he was at the protest site, police acted calmly and the government allowed peaceful protest, and that the road closure affected patients and workers.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Said the economic committee heard the transport minister and the drivers' association, whose accounts differed, and urged the government to answer drivers' unanswered letters and petition.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Said self-employed workers, including fishers, contractors and taxi drivers, face growing difficulty, asked about the promised taxi centre and requested extra debate time.

speakers.name: Ali Moosa
positions: Supported the resolution but said few resorts have the problem and it can be settled with industry and agencies.
Asked why the resolution's party, after five years in government with a majority, had not resolved it.

speakers.name: Ismail Nizar
positions: Said beards should not be a reason to refuse or lose resort jobs, and that other worker issues, such as foreign staff in senior posts and days off, also need attention.

speakers.name: Musthafa Hussain
positions: Presented the gang crimes bill: define gang and dangerous crimes, set penalties, monitor suspects, protect children and communities, and rehabilitate offenders.

speakers.name: Mohamed Fazeel
positions: Backed the bill as a sign of government attention to safety, citing a recent assault and saying it would address legal loopholes.

decisions: Parliament voted to take up the urgent matter on the taxi drivers' protest for debate (63 yes, 0 no, 0 abstentions, 64 present).
The chair declined a request to extend the one-hour debate time on the urgent matter and closed the debate.
Committee deadline of 27 February 2025 announced for the bill amending Law 7/2021 (higher education and training).
The President's letter on ministry work areas and the Minister of Tourism and Environment nomination were sent to the committee that reviews the government's responsibilities.
The President's letter on cutting base pay of heads of independent institutions by 10% was sent to the Finance Committee.
The Elections Commission president and vice-president nominations and the Anti-Corruption Commission vice-president nomination were sent to the Independent Institutions Committee.
The first reading of the bill amending the Decentralisation Act (Law 7/2010) was read.
The resolution on grooming and dress standards for tourism workers was accepted 60-0 and sent to the Economic Committee under rule 106(r).
The debate on the gang crimes bill was paused so the day's votes could be taken.
The next sitting was set for Tuesday 11 February 2025 at 9:00.
